artifact.canonical_name: Zonal Architecture Development with evolution of Artificial Intelligence

sources.title: Zonal Architecture Development with evolution of Artificial Intelligence
sources.role: Author paper/preprint used to verify the reported architecture, method/evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The paper characterizes zonal architecture as grouping devices by physical vehicle zones, using local/zonal controllers and a higher-speed backbone to reduce point-to-point wiring and support scalable sensor/actuator integration.

The authors describe zonal controllers as performing local preprocessing/decision functions while forwarding time-critical or higher-level workloads toward central vehicle computers, illustrating that zonal I/O distribution can coexist with centralized compute.
The paper discusses zonal architecture effects beyond data networking, including diagnostics and decentralized power distribution/power-management modules.
claims.context: Broad architecture discussion rather than a measured implementation.

limitations.text: The paper is primarily a narrative overview drawing on prior literature and does not present a controlled E/E architecture experiment that independently validates its broad performance, reliability, or cost claims.
A substantial part of the paper focuses on neural networks, autonomous driving, edge computing and sensor fusion; only the E/E responsibility-boundary portions are relevant to this survey.
Some broad assertions in the paper are stronger than the evidence shown; they should remain AUTHOR_CLAIM and not be repeated as established facts without stronger primary support.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Zonal Architecture Development with evolution of Artificial Intelligence; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full primary text verifies the paper's zonal-I/O/local-compute framing and its discussion of wiring, diagnostics and power distribution, while also showing that the contribution is a narrative overview rather than empirical validation.

editorial.why_now_note: It is directly on-topic and useful for tracing how practitioners describe zonal responsibilities, but stronger standards/industry/research sources should carry the report's core architecture claims.
editorial.rationale: Use as contextual synthesis, not as the sole evidence for zonal benefits or topology rules.
